points.text: Data collection continues: about thirty subjects were collected, ten dialogues are transcribed, and another cogsci student will play wizard in a more complicated round using psychology students.
Speaker C presented a simplified PRM with user, site, time, route and query classes and intermediate nodes that shrink the probability tables; it outputs a site desirability rating and an EVA mode.
Visitor Andy from the International University presented a smart FAQ and librarian system that uses context and ontologies to point to the right documents.
Speaker E suggests Andy look at FrameNet and talk to Dan Gildea, and Speaker D offers to take Andy to Gildea's office.
Speaker E says Eva will try to track down a PRM interpreter over the next few weeks, since the group will not build its own.
Speaker D wants to read the PRM write-up to check the details.
Speaker D is writing up the daily meeting discussions and revising the construal proposal, and may present it once Speaker E is back.
It is open whether a usable PRM interpreter exists, and whether PRM inference would be any faster than a flat Bayes-net.
How to specify structural uncertainty (probabilities on relations) in the PRM is unresolved; the plan is to work it out with Daphne's group when Daphne returns.
The SmartKom synthesis problems should be resolved but are not yet confirmed.
The group met after a break for an update on EDU, a PRM presentation, and a talk by visitor Andy on his content management research.
Data collection continues with a new wizard and a harder task design for psychology students.
Speaker C's PRM reuses user-side computation across sites, but she still sees no clear gain where outputs depend on both user and site.
Speaker E thinks the PRM is cleaner and fits ontology instances well, though inference may not be faster.
Andy wants a smart librarian that uses context to decide which questions to ask, and reuses existing ontologies rather than building everything himself.
Speaker E suggests FrameNet could help match documents to whole frames rather than individual keywords.
Speaker E describes the CITRIS state budget delay and a literacy tutoring idea from a CITRIS staffer.
Eva is to look for a PRM interpreter over the next few weeks.
Speaker D takes Andy to Dan Gildea's office.
Speaker D may present the revised construal proposal after Speaker E returns.
Thirty subjects were collected and ten dialogues are transcribed.
Speaker C built a simplified PRM with intermediate classes that make the probability tables easier to specify.
The SmartKom synthesis problems should be resolved as of this morning, according to Speaker D.
No PRM interpreter has been found yet, and the group will not build its own.
Speaker C still cannot see how the PRM helps when outputs depend on both user and site.
Speaker E says inference may not get faster with a PRM.
The synthesis fix is not yet confirmed, and may take more time.
A new cogsci student will play wizard in a more complicated data collection round using psychology students.
Speaker D and Johno meet tomorrow on the SmartKom synthesis issue.
Eva will look for a PRM interpreter over the next few weeks.
Speaker D is revising the construal proposal and may present it once Speaker E is back.
EDU data collection continues with a new wizard and a more complicated task for psychology students, after thirty subjects and ten transcribed dialogues.
Speaker C's simplified PRM outputs a site rating and an EVA mode, but progress depends on finding an interpreter, which Eva will look for.
Visitor Andy presented a smart FAQ and librarian system, and Speaker E suggested FrameNet and talking to Dan Gildea.
